source_evidence: Credit ratings seek to estimate the relative credit risk of a bond as compared with other bonds, although a high rating does not reflect a prediction that the bond has no chance of defaulting.
answer: Credit risk is the possibility that a municipal bond issuer has financial problems and cannot pay interest or principal in full; failure to pay is called default. A credit rating offers an estimate of the bond’s credit risk relative to other bonds. It is not a guarantee: even a highly rated bond can still default.
